construct: Hypobaric hypoxia stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors and increases ventilation, lowering PaCO2 and causing respiratory alkalosis. Over the next several days the kidneys increase bicarbonate excretion, reducing the alkalemic constraint on ventilatory drive and permitting sustained hyperventilation as acclimatization progresses.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: High-altitude hypoxemia stimulates sustained hyperventilation, causing hypocapnic respiratory alkalosis; over subsequent days the kidney lowers plasma bicarbonate by increasing bicarbonate excretion.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Increasing hydrogen secretion, ammonium excretion, or bicarbonate reabsorption would add or conserve systemic bicarbonate and therefore worsen rather than compensate for respiratory alkalosis.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only increased urinary bicarbonate excretion moves plasma bicarbonate in the compensatory direction while sustained hyperventilation persists.
